For grid B, I'm considering a single-yellow template with its own blue ring border, but I'm working through whether the matching logic requires the ring cells to be background-colored and the center yellow cell's exact recoloring behavior in the pattern check.

Reworking this: the least-frequent non-blue color (yellow vs black) determines the pattern, so the matcher keeps yellow cells and recolors the blue ring cells to background - meaning matches occur wherever a yellow shape sits with empty surroundings, then the full template (including its blue border) gets painted at those spots.

For variety across test grids, I'm planning different template shapes - an L-tromino, a vertical pair, a 2x2 square - and considering whether to include a rotated copy in one grid to test the full 8-fold symmetry, though that risks ambiguity if the solver doesn't infer rotation invariance. I'll keep the 2x2 square symmetric to avoid confusion, but let the vertical-pair grid implicitly test horizontal matches too, consistent with the earlier example.
